chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from more than one, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a Jew or a Christian who dies and has children who are not Muslims, he said: 'They are upon their inheritances.'
ai.seo_question: How is the inheritance of a non-Muslim parent distributed among their non-Muslim children according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the children of a non-Muslim parent inherit according to their father's specific religious law (millah), rather than applying Islamic inheritance rules. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of respecting the internal legal systems of Ahl al-Kitab in matters of personal status, provided they are not Muslim. It underscores the flexibility in applying religious law to non-Muslims within their own communities.
